records.reason: m66 at 2/1 and 100 uL supplies a stronger-eluent point below the severe 5/1 miss in observed 49201b5817f204116f7f. It locates the onset transition for pyridyl ketones and tests whether the late response persists under stronger eluent.

m66 at 0/1 and matched loading extends the same response curve toward the strongest eluent. Comparing this with observed 49201b5817f204116f7f distinguishes a localized threshold from a blanket upward correction for aromatic nitrogen.

m141 at 10/1 and 150 uL is an interior point between observed 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9 at 5/1 and 51f4126a3aadb3239225 at 20/1. It directly tests the model's predicted late transition for lutidine under fixed loading.

m141 at 2/1 adds a stronger-eluent anchor to the same scaffold and tests whether its unexpectedly late behavior begins only near 5/1 or is already present at 2/1. The contrast is motivated by observed 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9 and 51f4126a3aadb3239225.

m216 at 2/1 and 100 uL extends the quinoline curve below observed 33ffc69a253a89f15995 at 5/1 and 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321 at 10/1 with fixed loading. This should repair the location and slope of the fused-base response.

m216 at 0/1 provides the strongest-eluent endpoint for the same loading regime. Together with observed 33ffc69a253a89f15995 and 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321, it tests whether the learned quinoline correction extrapolates to the low-retention end.

m211 at 10/1 and 50 uL fills the major gap between observed ecd17c7ea435a1e33f6b at 2/1, 292e0342682192a69fce at 5/1, and 434e465cfa7e0034f233 at 20/1. The matched loading makes this a high-value curve-shape measurement.

m146 at 1/1 supplies a still stronger-eluent anchor near the curve boundary. Its value comes from distinguishing a gradual quinoline response from the sharp transition suggested by observed cf36dbeee8bb51632d84, 04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12, and 9e3ce3497298084abd83.

m160 at 2/1 and 50 uL tests whether the late aminobenzonitrile response seen at 5/1 in observed b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 begins under stronger eluent. It is also one half of an exact amount contrast with the selected 150 uL row.

m161 at 1/1 and 100 uL probes the stronger-eluent side of the positional isomer whose 5/1 label was very late in observed 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e. This tests whether the learned correction is positional and condition dependent.

m88 at 2/1 and 100 uL is a matched-loading stronger-eluent point below the severe 5/1 label in observed d2921349ba8d9cef15a4. It tests the response boundary for the aminoester environment rather than transferring the 5/1 correction uniformly.

m202 at 1/1 and 100 uL samples the strong-eluent side of the phosphorus response. Observed 86258f5c8ffdb874521f at 5/1 and 902937db42f82f467718 at 10/1 show a steep transition, so this point can locate its lower boundary.

m202 at 2/1 and matched loading directly brackets the steep rise between observed 86258f5c8ffdb874521f at 5/1 and 902937db42f82f467718 at 10/1. It should teach the model a local phosphorus ratio response instead of an average correction.

m199 at 0/1 and 50 uL extends the sulfone curve below observed 9ddc2e8babb52ee8e772 at 2/1 and f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c at 5/1. This tests whether retention approaches an early regime under the strongest eluent.

m181 at 10/1 and 100 uL is a response-curve point below the unexpectedly late 20/1 label in observed 10ea0c665f5ba7c91bbf. It tests whether the cyclic lactone transition is gradual or concentrated at higher PE/EA.

m181 at 2/1 and 50 uL provides a stronger-eluent anchor for the unsupported cyclic lactone environment. The label can distinguish a low-ratio early regime from the large V1/V2 miss in observed 10ea0c665f5ba7c91bbf.

m200 at 1/1 and 50 uL is an interior point below the severe 2/1 result in observed a92f7617b135de150588, with the same loading solvent and volume. It tests how quickly the nitro alcohol becomes retained.

m200 at 0/1 and 50 uL supplies the strongest-eluent counterpart to the selected 1/1 row and observed a92f7617b135de150588. This discriminates a sharp nitro/OH threshold from a smooth polarity-based trend.

m204 at 1/1 and 50 uL adds a stronger-eluent boundary point to observed 45a1b11ae63f2dab2e48 and 73502a52708e4f9c2391. The result can separate a gradual alcohol curve from a threshold response.

m28 at 2/1 and 100 uL probes the low-ratio side of the aromatic ester-aldehyde curve after the V2 underprediction at 5/1 in observed 050e2fab4b407ea058cb and the large 10/1 miss in db7f9ffa50eb931613f6.

m28 at 1/1 and 150 uL adds a stronger-eluent point with substantial loading. Together with observed 050e2fab4b407ea058cb and db7f9ffa50eb931613f6, it tests whether V2 rises smoothly or turns on over a narrow ratio interval.

m107 at 1/1 and 100 uL tests the lower-ratio and loading dependence of a beta-ketoester whose observed 5/1 labels in c6924324ddd95f249df6 and 2cfa393cb79664e100ce were already late. It provides a common scaffold-condition relationship for retraining.

m94 at 10/1 and 100 uL is a matched-ratio amount contrast to the observed 10/1, 150 uL label 5b445b457a8b897a2d6c and complements the broader m94 observations ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f and ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4.

m90 at 2/1 and 100 uL tests transfer from the late aminoester and aminobenzonitrile regions observed in 9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb, d2921349ba8d9cef15a4, and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90. Its intermediate condition is useful for deciding whether pyridyl ester geometry follows the same correction.

m90 at 0/1 and 50 uL supplies a strong-eluent endpoint for the same nitrogen-containing ester environment. It tests whether the suspected late response is intrinsic or appears only after a ratio-dependent transition suggested by observed 9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb and d2921349ba8d9cef15a4.

m38 at 10/1 and 150 uL tests the lower-ratio response of acetylfluorene after the large underprediction at 20/1 in observed 8f9a7ca0380c405ee685. This covers fused-ring carbonyl placement and a loading contrast relevant to generalization.

m165 at 10/1 and 100 uL extends the chalcone response below observed a7f8c888870123f3b277 at 20/1 and complements the matched structural contrast with m164 in b7fffd840d208b29776c. It tests whether the model learned the curve location as well as the structural difference.

m193 at 5/1 and 100 uL tests the lower-ratio response of a nitroaldehyde related to the late observed 10/1 label df6457ca86c98c073bf6. This helps distinguish a nitro-specific V2 correction from a broader aldehyde correction.

m160 at 2/1 and 150 uL is the exact loading counterpart to the selected 50 uL m160 row. Holding ratio, density, solvent, and loading-solvent volume fixed makes this a direct amount-effect experiment in the newly identified late nitrogen region.

m86 at 1/1 and 150 uL extends the aminoester response below observed 9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb at 5/1 with identical loading. It tests where this positional aminoester enters its late regime and whether the m86 and m88 corrections transfer.

hypotheses.content: Loading effects are scaffold- and endpoint-specific. Late V2 persists across measured amounts for m107, m13, m94, and m37, while m177 shows substantially different amount sensitivity; high loading alone does not explain the broad late-V2 failures.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The exact m160 amount pair can teach whether the new nitrogen failure region has a loading interaction and can prevent the retrained model from conflating amount effects with structure effects.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed ratio and loading solvent, does changing amount shift V1 and V2 together for aromatic amines, or mainly alter the onset endpoint?

hypotheses.content: Beta-ketoester solvent-response curves are scaffold-specific; the predicted flattening for m82 and m95 is weakened by their measured late V2 values, while m94 and m107 show substantial ratio-dependent growth.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m94 and m107 points test whether the model can learn separate ratio and loading responses rather than applying a universal beta-ketoester trend.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m94 10/1 amount contrast and the m107 1/1 point preserve late V2, or does either scaffold show a distinct lower-ratio regime?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol, phenol, and nitro-alcohol retention depends on local structural context and has scaffold-specific ratio thresholds. The latest m60, m67, m99, m205, m200, and m204 labels do not support a single OH or polarity correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Adjacent-ratio measurements on m200 and m204 test whether the graph model learns local thresholds and V1/V2 separately, which should transfer to other oxygenated rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the stronger-eluent m200 and m204 labels show a common onset boundary, or do nitro substitution and hydroxyalkyl topology produce separate curves?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen environment and solvent ratio jointly govern retention. Fused aromatic bases, pyridyl ketones, lutidine, quinoline, and phenylpyridine occupy related but nonidentical late-retention regimes with different transition locations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This is the largest measured failure region. Matched-loading ratio points across m66, m141, m146, m211, and m216 can repair condition-response mapping across many aromatic nitrogen rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where is the ratio-dependent retention transition for each nitrogen environment, and which parts of the correction transfer across fused bases, pyridyl ketones, and simple aryl pyridines?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl attachment, conjugation, fused-ring geometry, and neighboring oxygen placement produce two-sided prediction failures and distinct V1/V2 response curves.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m28, m38, m165, m181, and m193 selections cover distinct graph environments where the current model has underpredicted V2 or misplaced the curve, improving structural transfer beyond descriptor similarity.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which carbonyl and oxygen geometries share a learnable V2 correction, and which require separate local graph representations?

hypotheses.content: Sulfoxide and phosphorus-containing environments have steep, locally structured ratio responses rather than a simple upward retention offset; the sulfone m199 curve also changes rapidly between 2/1 and 5/1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected m199 and m202 points locate steep transitions and teach the retrained model how to interpolate sparse functional-group-specific response curves.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the strong transition begin near 2/1, 5/1, or only closer to 10/1 for each electron-rich sulfur or phosphorus environment?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic amines, aminobenzonitriles, and aminoesters show local graph and positional effects that can produce unexpectedly late V2; descriptor-level similarity to ordinary esters or pyridines is insufficient.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m86, m88, m160, m161, and m90 selections test whether the model can represent local amine, cyano, ester, and positional interactions and their ratio boundaries.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do stronger-eluent labels reveal a shared late-retention threshold across these nitrogen-rich motifs, or separate positional and functional-group-specific curves?

feedback_interpretation: Recent labels strengthened the nitrogen failure diagnosis: m66, m86, m88, m160, and m161 were much later than predicted at sampled conditions, while m141 remained extremely late at 20/1. The m146 and m216 labels provide useful curve anchors but leave transition locations unresolved. The m82 and m95 outcomes weakened the earlier predicted beta-ketoester flattening, whereas m200, m181, m204, m28, and m38 confirmed substantial local oxygen and nitro-environment errors. Measurements for m199 and m202 now demonstrate steep ratio transitions. The new batch therefore emphasizes adjacent-ratio points at matched loading, includes an exact m160 amount pair, and uses a few related nitrogen and carbonyl rows to test transfer rather than applying blanket corrections.
batch_rationale: The batch repairs the largest observed error region with ratio curves for pyridyl ketone, lutidine, quinoline, methylquinoline, and phenylpyridine. Aminobenzonitrile and aminoester selections extend the same repair into local amine and cyano environments, including a fixed-ratio m160 amount pair that separates loading from structural effects. Separate curves for m199, m202, m181, m200, and m204 locate steep or newly exposed transitions. m28, m38, m165, m193, m94, and m107 cover carbonyl and oxygen arrangements where V2 has been underpredicted or loading interactions remain unclear. The batch combines failure repair with targeted structural transfer and a small amount of exploration, giving the retrained model information about condition-response shape, endpoint-specific behavior, and graph environments represented across many remaining Row-distribution conditions.
